articles.title: Where is Spain headed after the snap election announcement?
articles.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is taking a gamble by calling an early election in Spain. The housing crisis, migration and the rise of the right-wing populist Vox party are all likely to dominate the…

image.caption: Early on Monday morning, Prime Minister Sanchez announced snap parliamentary electionsImage: LA MONCLOA/AFP

blocks.text: Spain's economic data has been positive recently, but politically, the country has been mired in a prolonged crisis for months.
On Monday, the social democratic Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez responded with a surprise move to break the deadlock: He is calling an early election for November 29.
Why is Sanchez calling an election now?

The sudden announcement followed a dramatic political defeat for the government. On Friday, October 2, Sanchez's emergency measures to tackle the housing crisis failed in parliament. Seven lawmakers from the conservative Catalan separatist party Junts, whose support the government has relied on since 2023, brought the measures down. Sanchez says he is now calling for a "much broader progressive majority."

blocks.caption: Set to profit from the snap election: Vox leader Santiago AbascalImage: Gabriela Sardá Núñez/Europa Press/IMAGO

blocks.text: The defeat came after months of growing instability in the government's parliamentary base. Spain's parliament has not passed a regular budget since 2023.

The recent crisis over mass migration to Ceuta and several corruption scandals involving allegations against the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE) and people close to Sanchez have piled pressure onto the government.
And then came Maricarmen. The forced eviction of 87-year-old Maria del Carmen Abascal last month suddenly turned the housing shortage into the headline political issue.
The fact that his emergency measures were rejected in parliament allows Sanchez to position himself as a defender of tenants. However, it remains to be seen whether that strategy will pay off.
What role is pressure from the street protests playing?

The housing shortage has been at the top of Spaniards' list of concerns for around three years. According to estimates by the Bank of Spain, the country is currently short of around 750,000 homes, and the figure could exceed one million by 2028.

More than half of 18- to 34-year-olds live with their parents or depend on them financially. Property prices have recently been rising three times as fast as wages. In Spain, social housing accounts for just around 1.7 percent of the country's housing stock, putting it at the lower end of the EU scale in comparison with other member states.
Housing crisis triggers snap election in Spain

It is hardly surprising, then, that protest camps sprang up in Madrid and elsewhere in response to the plight of Maricarmen Abascal, and tens of thousands took to the streets across the country. After the government's measures were rejected, the trade unions CCOO and UGT even announced a 24-hour general strike.

These dividing lines, however, do not simply split the government and the opposition. The tenants' movement also views Sanchez's plans as insufficient. The conservative opposition People's Party (PP) and parts of the business community, meanwhile, warn that tighter rent controls could make the problem worse.
Is Sanchez's model of governance coming to an end?

Since the 2023 election, Pedro Sanchez has governed without a majority in parliament. His social democratic PSOE formed a coalition with the left-wing Sumar alliance, but also depended on the support of smaller parties. These included Basque and Catalan regional parties, but above all the Catalan separatists of Junts.

That meant its seven lawmakers were repeatedly able to determine whether government legislation secured a majority or not. Over the course of the parliamentary term, this arrangement became increasingly unstable. In the first half of 2026 alone, the government lost almost one in four votes.

blocks.caption: For three years, the government has failed to get a budget through parliamentImage: Elisabetta Trevisan/Vatican Media/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Evidence of the extent of this political deadlock is the state budget: Spain continues to work with the 2023 budget because the prime minister has been unable to get a new budget through parliament in his entire term. Junts ultimately refused to support Sanchez on housing policy, leaving him without backing on an issue that has been at the top of the political agenda following nationwide protests.
What was the political fallout of the Ceuta crisis?

At the end of July, more than 70,000 people crossed the border from Morocco into Ceuta within a short period of time. Although the government declared the crisis over soon afterward, at least 10,000 migrants were still in the exclave two months later, which has a population of only around 80,000. It was not until last Sunday that police cleared an improvised camp where around 3,000 people had been living.
Spain: Tensions in aftermath of Ceuta mass migrant crossing

The crisis altered Sanchez's previously relatively liberal migration policy. A new draft seen by Reuters proposes accelerated asylum procedures and deportations, as well as tighter rules. Human rights organizations have voiced sharp criticism.
How strong is the opposition?
At first glance, Spain's conservative PP is entering the snap parliamentary election at the end of November as the frontrunner to become the largest parliamentary group.

The real winner of recent months, however, is the right-wing populist Vox party. It is now polling at just over 18%, around six percentage points more than in the 2023 election. A strong Vox turnout could increase PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo's chances of gathering enough seats for a governing majority from parties right of center.

blocks.caption: The man hoping to become Spain's next prime minister: PP leader Alberto Nunez FeijooImage: Burak Akbulut/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: Vox leader Santiago Abascal is now confidently setting conditions for cooperation. Priority for Spanish citizens, economic deregulation and a significantly tougher migration policy, including the far-right concept of deporting foreign nationals to their countries of origin.

For his part, Feijoo faces a difficult balancing act. To replace Sanchez, he also needs to win voters from the political center. At the same time, he may need a partner for a governing majority who is steering the campaign significantly further to the right.
Will Spain also be voting on Trump and Europe's political direction?

In international media coverage, Sanchez is repeatedly portrayed as Europe's most prominent critic of Donald Trump. The prime minister rejected the US president's demand for defense spending to rise to 5% of GDP, refused to allow US bases in Spain to be used for the war against Iran and criticized US-Israeli attacks.

As a result, Trump even threatened at one point to cut off trade relations. At the same time, Sanchez explicitly contrasts his more liberal migration policy with Trump's deportation policies and attacks what he calls the "tech oligarchs" from the United States.

blocks.caption: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez (left) has positioned himself as a strong European voice against Donald TrumpImage: Pablo Martinez Monsivais/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Sanchez is also one of the most prominent social democratic leaders of a major EU country. If the left were to lose the upcoming Spanish election, the European Council would lose one of its most outspoken voices against Donald Trump . It would also lose a prime minister who has opposed climbing defense spending, defended a more liberal approach to migration and criticized Israel more sharply over the war in Gaza than most of his European counterparts.
This article originally appeared in German.

articles.title: Pornhub returns to Australia but only for adults with Apple devices
articles.summary: The world's most popular porn site went dark in March in Australia due to age verification laws.

blocks.text: Pornhub has returned to Australia, eight months after it went dark due to age verification laws, but only adults with Apple devices will be able to access the site.
On Wednesday, parent company Aylo said it was restoring access for "eligible adult users in Australia" who have "confirmed their age through Apple's Australian age-verification process".

The world's biggest porn site left the Australian market in March, saying new laws requiring users to prove they were over 18 would not protect children and "instead creates harms relating to data privacy" and exposure to content on non-compliant platforms.
Apple recently introduced new age checks in Australia, following a rollout in the UK.
In March, Australia introduced stricter laws requiring users to prove they were over 18 in order to access adult content such as porn, R-rated video games and sexually explicit AI chatbots.
The country's online safety regulator said the changes would protect children from harmful content and platforms would be fined for breaches.
Critics said there would be issues with data privacy and users finding ways to trick age-verification technologies such as facial recognition, digital IDs and credit card details.
Aylo said it was returning to Australia as Apple has "set a benchmark" by setting default child safety features on all devices unless owners confirmed they are adults.
This, in effect, makes "every phone or tablet kid-safe as a starting point," it said.

"For years, Aylo has advocated for device-based age verification as the most effective and privacy-protecting approach to help prevent minors from accessing age-inappropriate content online," said Aylo's vice-president of brand and community Alex Kekesi.
Australians with Apple devices that have been "age-verified" will be "served a standard adult users experience", she said.
Kekesi added that having devices with child safety features as a default meant adults don't have to "surrender unnecessary personal information to multiple apps and websites".
It also limits the usefulness of virtual private networks (VPNs) to circumvent age-verification technologies, she said.
VPNs are commonly used to trick a site into thinking a user is logging on from another country, giving the user access to the site.

articles.title: EU negotiators head to China hoping to curb cheap imports of hybrid electric cars
articles.summary: Mood in trade talks said to have changed as EU member states harden demands for protection against Chinese imports EU trade negotiators are heading to China for two days of crunch talks aimed at…

blocks.text: EU trade negotiators are heading to China for two days of crunch talks aimed at sealing a breakthrough deal tackling Beijing’s record £1bn-a-day trade surplus by curbing its exports of cheap hybrid electric cars into Europe.
Trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and his team fly out on Wednesday and will be negotiating up to the wire in talks scheduled to start the following day and continue late into Friday.
Sources say they hope to achieve “tangible, meaningful and measurable” results before the meeting of EU leaders in Brussels on Thursday next week, where China is high on the agenda.

The main focus is on what has been described as a “proof of concept” pilot agreement involving one sector, which is expected to be cars, which could be scaled up for other sectors in the coming months.

Diplomatic efforts to avert a full-scale trade war started at the end of June, albeit with little hope that China could curb exports to the EU given its historic ability to pivot quickly any time trade barriers are put in its path. For example, after the EU imposed tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles in October 2024 there was a boom in exports of hybrid cars, which were not subject to tariffs.
Last month, the EU asked China to voluntarily restrict hybrid exports to address soaring sales, warning that if they did not restrict them, safeguards – which could include quotas – could be enacted.

It is not known what China’s response was. But sources say the mood in talks has changed as EU member states have hardened demands for protection against Chinese imports that threaten their own industries.

On Monday, Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, agreed a “historic U-turn” on its policy on China by siding with the French president, Emmanuel Macron, in authorising effective permission for EU leaders to approve a new instrument to allow them to defend trade by cutting access to the single market at short notice.

In a joint paper with Emmanuel Macron, the two countries spoke of “a massive industrial shock … affecting sectors at the heart of the European industrial model and of systemic relevance [pharmaceuticals, aerospace, automotive, machine tools, chemicals, etc.]”.

The paper called for the use of all existing trade defence tools, but also for a new diversification instrument and “possible additional” new measures to allow the bloc to react when “third countries seek to undermine the restoration of a level playing field”.

Andrew Small, a former EU adviser on China, said Šefčovič’s talks will test the resolve of both Beijing and Brussels and will “determine whether China is willing to put sufficiently serious offers on the table”.

Small, who is the Asia director at the European Council on Foreign Relations in Berlin, warned: “China’s most effective tactic may be to draw Europe into a ‘process trap’ offering just enough to delay action, without addressing the forces driving European deindustrialisation.”
after newsletter promotion

Sources say the Franco-German proposals for a new instrument, dubbed a “kill switch”, were born out of frustration, particularly in Paris, that a so-called “trade bazooka” available to Brussels, officially known as the anti-coercion instrument, has never been used.
Paris pushed for the use of the ACI following Trump’s threat of tariffs last year but it never gained traction from others as it could take up to a year to implement.

Handlesblatt, the Germany business newspaper, described Monday’s change in policy as “nothing less than an economic turning point”, with chief political reporter Martin Greive concluding in a hard-hitting column that Merz was “putting an end to years of naiveté towards Beijing”.

“Merz has recognised in recent months that Germany is the epicentre of the China shock 2.0; that there might not be much left of German industry if Germany continues to stand by and watch as China gains enormous export advantages through trillions in subsidies, the unilateral siphoning off of knowhow, and a – to put it mildly – questionable monetary policy,” he wrote.

articles.title: France’s Mistral launches AI model it says outperforms some Chinese rivals
articles.summary: Mistral Large 4 will be made publicly available on October 27

blocks.text: MISTRAL. An advertisement for Mistral AI, the French artificial intelligence company, is displayed inside the Grand Central subway station in New York City, USA, on May 21, 2026.
Shannon Stapleton/Reuters
Mistral Large 4 will be made publicly available on October 27

items: French AI startup Mistral launched a new AI model, Mistral Large 4, claiming it outperforms many rival open-weight models, including certain Chinese models.
The model will be publicly available on October 27, with a version for cybersecurity experts and government authorities to test beforehand.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

PARIS, France – French AI startup Mistral unveiled a new AI model on Tuesday, October 6, ending a gap of about five months between major releases, and said it outperforms many rival open-weight models.

The three-year-old company, widely viewed as Europe’s strongest AI challenger to US and Chinese competitors, has not released a new model since May. In August, it began offering third-party models to customers, starting with Beijing-based Z.ai’s GLM 5.3.

“The model we’re actually announcing today is actually above the Chinese models on certain aspects, including cyber. So the narrative that Europe cannot compete is something that is not true,” CEO Artur Mensch said at a launch event in Abu Dhabi, without specifying which Chinese models or benchmarks he was referring to.
Mistral said Le Chonk, officially named Mistral Large 4, will be made publicly available on October 27.
Before the release, cybersecurity experts and government authorities will be given access to a version with fewer safety restrictions to test its capabilities, the company said.
Pierre Stock, Mistral’s vice president of science, told Reuters that the model ranks among the strongest open-weight, systems available.

Open-weight means users can download the model from platforms and run it on their own hardware. Many Chinese models are open-weight, while top US models tend to be closed and accessible only through their developers’ infrastructure.
Stock told Reuters the model had tried to go beyond its testing environment, but that this was expected and the company was able to prevent it.
OpenAI and Anthropic, whose most advanced models have demonstrated similar behaviour in testing, have restricted access to their most cyber-capable systems.
After executives at US AI companies warned last month that AI could pose an existential threat to humanity, Mensch dismissed such arguments as self-serving.
Mistral, which raised €3 billion ($3.4 billion) in its latest funding round, has positioned itself as a safer, European alternative.
Mistral said Large 4 is “closing the gap with frontier models” in areas including coding, finance, geospatial analysis, manufacturing and product design.
The company trained the model on its own infrastructure.
Stock said Mistral’s goal was to partner “very deeply” with backers including ASML and new-investor Samsung “across the entire value chain”.
He said Large 4 is capable of designing computer chips, but declined to comment on whether Mistral is currently working with Samsung on chip development. – Rappler.com

MANILA, Philippines – Have you ever received a suspicious text, encountered an online offer that seemed too good to be true, or wondered if a shared link was legitimate?
From fake QR payment codes targeting everyday consumers to increasingly sophisticated AI-generated misinformation, knowing how to spot digital red flags and protect yourself matters more than ever.

blocks.caption: [Tech Thoughts] Better discernment needed as Filipinos among most targeted by digital fraud

blocks.text: To help Filipinos navigate these evolving digital threats, Rappler — in partnership with SmartCT, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Laguna, and the City Government of San Pedro — is bringing its “#ScamAlert” campaign to San Pedro, Laguna. The initiative aims to equip citizens with essential digital safety skills and empower communities to combat online fraud.

The event, titled “#ScamAlert: Maging Wais, Maging Ligtas,” will take place on Monday, October 19, from 1 pm to 4 pm, at the Pacita Astrodome in San Pedro, Laguna. Both in-person and virtual participation options are available.
The event is part of Scam Ready ASEAN, an ASEAN regional programme supported by Google.org and implemented by the ASEAN Foundation.
The program features insightful discussions with experts and community partners, alongside interactive sessions to help attendees build confidence in identifying online threats.
Attendees will also get hands-on experience with the “Be Scam Ready” gameplay activity and explore practical tools, reporting channels, and resources to take action against fraud.
Attendance is free and open to the public. However, on-site seats are limited, so pre-registration is required. Virtual attendees must also register in advance to receive the live stream link.

Confirmed in-person attendees will receive confirmation emails containing event reminders and instructions.
Participants must also download the Rappler app ahead of the event and join the Scam Alert chat room on Muni, an online community space and network in the Rappler app.
Scam Alert is a space to report scams and find practical guidance on how to respond, warn others, and flag incidents to the relevant authorities.

articles.title: Former Australian bishop jailed for sexually abusing young men
articles.summary: The former Bishop of Broome is one of the most senior Catholic clerics in the world to face charges of this nature.

blocks.text: Former Australian bishop Christopher Saunders has been jailed for sexually abusing two young Aboriginal men during his time as a Catholic cleric.
Saunders - who resigned as Bishop of Broome when first accused of wrongdoing in 2020 - was found guilty of one charge of rape and 12 counts of indecent assault.
The 76-year-old was sentenced to six and a half years' imprisonment, but will be eligible for release on parole in February 2031.
He is one of the most senior Catholic leaders in the world to face charges of this nature.

His trial in the state of Western Australia heard Saunders systematically groomed the two young men, inviting them to "shirts-off" gatherings and plying them with alcohol, often using church funds and church-owned properties to do so.
He was convicted of kissing and molesting the men, and in one instance forcing oral sex on one of them.
In a victim impact statement provided to the court, that young man said he struggled to talk about what happened.
"I was a toy that he was using," the victim said.
"My head is pounding now, I'm in so much pain."

articles.title: Jobless Filipinos drop to 2.77 million in August
articles.summary: The number of jobless Filipinos in August this year declined to 2.77 million, indicating a 5.3% drop in the unemployment rate from July’s 6%.

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 11:16am

Individuals flock to the Provincial Training and Development Center II at the Capitol Complex in Lingayen, Pangasinan to apply for jobs offered by various companies at the Labor Day Job Fair on May 1, 2026.
The STAR / Cesar Ramirez
MANILA, Philippines — The number of jobless Filipinos in August this year declined to 2.77 million, indicating a 5.3% drop in the unemployment rate from July’s 6%.

The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported on Wednesday, October 6, that the number of unemployed individuals in the country dropped from July’s 3.14 million but remains higher than the record from the same period last year.
According to the state’s data agency, the unemployment rate in August 2025 stood at 3.9%, or 2.03 million jobless individuals.
National Statistician Claire Dennis Mapa said in a press briefing on Wednesday that the decline was driven by fewer individuals entering the labor force.
“In terms of new entrants, mas konti ngayong pumasok ng August kaysa sa pumasok noong Hulyo,” Mapa said.
(In terms of new entrants, fewer people entered in August than in July.)
Compared with July, when 1.5 million Filipinos entered the labor force, only about 897,000 individuals joined the workforce in August. Of this, 470,000 became employed, while 427,000 were unemployed.
The statistics agency also recorded a higher labor force participation rate in August at 64%, higher than the rate in July, which stood at 63.6%.

The labor force refers to individuals 15 years old and above who are either employed or unemployed. The labor force participation rate in August translates to a total of 52.56 million Filipinos, slightly higher than the 52.36 million in July and the 52.13 million in the same month last year.
Higher employment rate
The employment rate, meanwhile, slightly increased to 94.7% in August compared to July’s 94%.
The rate translates to 49.79 million Filipinos having jobs, which is higher than the 49.21 million recorded in July.
The data agency noted, however, that it is lower than the 96.1% record, or 50.10 million individuals, in August 2025.

Most of the employed individuals came from the services sector, with a 61.7% share, or 30.72 million individuals, followed by the agriculture sector with 20.9%, or 10.43 million people, and the industry sector with 17.3%, or 8.64 million Filipinos.
Bad weather, less work hours. The average weekly working hours of employed individuals in August also went down to around 39.2 hours from around 40.6 hours in July and 41 hours in August 2025.
Mapa said that among the main factors that contributed to the shorter weekly work hours in August were inclement weather conditions and flooding that led to work suspensions.

“Ang malaki talaga na rason ay ‘yung bad weather. So medyo bumaba ‘yung hours worked per week ng mga employed persons dahil ni-reason nila na bad weather and alam natin noong August masyadong maraming araw na malalakas ang ulan at meron tayong pagbaha,” Mapa said.

(The main reason was really bad weather. So, the hours worked per week of employed persons declined because they cited bad weather as the reason, and we know that in August, there were many days of heavy rains and flooding.)

articles.title: Security Council to probe China funds linked to Sara Duterte
articles.summary: National Security Adviser Eduardo Oban Jr. said that the allegations, which emerged during the ongoing impeachment proceedings, may have national security implications.

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 11:07am
In this photo uploaded on Facebook on June 26, 2026 shows Vice President Sara Duterte.
Vice President Sara Duterte via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — The National Security Council (NSC) announced that it will conduct an investigation into reports of foreign financial inflows from China directed toward companies linked to the family of Vice President Sara Duterte.

In a statement on Tuesday, October 6, National Security Adviser Eduardo Oban Jr. said that the allegations, which emerged during the ongoing impeachment proceedings, may have national security implications.

“While the proceedings remain ongoing and the information presented should be properly examined within established legal processes, the reported transactions and any credible information involving significant foreign financial flows that may bear upon the country's national security warrants careful, in-depth, and responsible assessment,” the NSC said.

“The NSC will look into the information presented and, as a matter of policy, continue to task the intelligence and investigative agencies and coordinate with relevant government institutions to assess the national security implications, if any, arising from the reported transactions,” it added.

Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura testified on Day 33 of the impeachment trial that Cale88 Foods Corp., a firm tied to Vice President Duterte’s husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, received P319 million in remittances from China and Hong Kong.
Meanwhile, former senator Antonio Trillanes IV alleged during a Friday press briefing that the couple accepted separate payments of P150 million and P319 million through their respective entities.
The Chinese Embassy in Manila denied the allegations, saying that Beijing has never funneled funds to any Philippine political faction.

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon didn’t talk about Jesse Baird to friend in lead-up to alleged murders, court hears
articles.summary: NSW police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering his ex and Luke Davies in a Sydney terrace in February 2024 Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Despite an alleged…

blocks.text: Despite an alleged obsession with his ex, Beau Lamarre-Condon never spoke about him to a close friend in the three months before allegedly murdering him, a jury has heard.
Lamarre-Condon, 31, has pleaded not guilty to murdering his ex-partner Jesse Baird and the man’s new boyfriend Luke Davies in a Sydney terrace in February 2024.

The former senior constable says the two men died in two separate violent struggles with him over his police pistol, and his subsequent efforts to dispose of their bodies were indicative of his panic about the unexpected deaths.
Much evidence in the NSW supreme court trial’s first three weeks has centred on Lamarre-Condon’s alleged growing obsession with Baird in the year leading up to the killings.
The prosecution alleges the then-police officer became infatuated with Baird after they broke off contact in November 2023, resolving to murder him.
However, Lamarre-Condon’s close friend Nicole Harvell told the court on Wednesday she could not remember any conversation with the ex-officer about Baird after the pair broke up for the final time.
That was despite her being in almost daily contact with the now-31-year-old.

blocks.caption: Evidence and testimony in week two of Beau Lamarre-Condon’s trial – video

blocks.text: Harvell, a police senior constable, recalled trying to contact her friend when she saw media reports that he was under suspicion for the two men’s deaths.
“Fuck Beau, are you ok?” she texted to Lamarre-Condon’s phone.
She never received a reply.
The sworn officer maintained under cross-examination that the accused killer had months earlier told her about enlisting his mother to help him lie to Baird.
Lamarre-Condon posted an Instagram story with a bunch of flowers and the caption: “When he’s in Melbourne but still sends you these.”
after newsletter promotion
But publication was restricted to select friends that did not include Baird.
The photo was designed to imply Baird had sent flowers to the accused, despite the pair not being in a relationship at the time, Harvell said.
When Baird discovered the ruse, Lamarre-Condon spent $160 on a bouquet identical to the photo to lie to him, the officer’s friend said.
Lamarre-Condon then sent a photo to Baird showing his mother with the fresh bouquet.
The bouquet had a handwritten note to imply his mother had been the intended recipient and they were from her partner, who was in Melbourne, the jury heard.
“I recall the accused telling me his mother had written that note,” Harvell said.
The trial continues.

articles.title: Mali: Junta forces retake strategic town of Kidal from separatists
articles.summary: Mali's military regained control of the strategic town of Kidal after forcing Tuareg separatists and al Queda-linked jihadists to withdraw following an offensive backed by Russia's Africa Corps.

image.caption: Malian troops ⁠were "reinforcing ⁠their presence" in the town by Tuesday night, a government statement said [FILE: May 9, 2026]Image: AFP

blocks.text: Mali's army, supported by Russian paramilitary forces, has re-entered the northern town of Kidal, forcing the Tuareg separatists to withdraw from the strategic hold, in a symbolic boost for the country's military government and its Russian allies.

The Tuareg separatist Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) said in a statement it had "decided to carry out a strategic and controlled withdrawal of its forces from the town of Kidal." It said the withdrawal took place without direct fighting.
This followed the "disproportionate use of aerial assets by Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps," according to an FLA spokesperson.
How did Kidal fall earlier this year?
The FLA and al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) seized Kidal during a series of attacks earlier this year in April that also killed Mali's defense minister.
Tuareg separatists from the Azawad Liberation Front have been fighting for years to create an independent state in northern Mali.
Mali's junta, which came to power in back-to-back coups in 2020 and 2021, has increasingly relied on Russian paramilitary support against fighters linked to al-Qaeda and the Islamic State.

blocks.caption: Mali's junta in recent years distanced itself from former colonial power France and deepened military and political ties with Russia [FILE: May 9, 2026]Image: AFP

blocks.text: What does Kidal's recapture mean for Mali's junta?
Analysts say the latest advance is largely a symbolic victory for Mali's junta.

"A successful recapture... affirms the military-led government's authority and boosts the army's morale, particularly after several high-profile setbacks both in the north and the central regions in recent weeks," Beverly Ochieng, associate director of Control Risks, told Reuters.
Ochieng, however, added the retaking of Kidal is largely "symbolic" and not "decisive" in Mali's campaign against jihadist and separatist groups.
Human rights organizations have often accused the Malian army and Russian paramilitaries of killing civilians during military operations, with all sides also accused of committing war crimes.

articles.title: Football: Lionel Messi plays final game for Argentina
articles.summary: Argentinian superstar Lionel Messi bowed out of international football with one last goal for his country. For football in Argentina, and indeed across the world, it's the end of an era.

image.caption: Argentinian fans have long worshipped Messi as the successor to the great Diego MaradonaImage: Gustavo Garello/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Lionel Messi made his 208th and final appearance for Argentina on Tuesday night, scoring his 126th and final international goal as the Albiceleste beat Benin 3-0 in a friendly in Buenos Aires.
In emotional scenes at a packed El Monumental stadium, Messi stepped up to convert a penalty in the 71st minute, prompting wild celebrations from teammates and fans alike.

Earlier, the 39-year-old superstar had already set up goals for teammates Nicolas Otamendi – who was also making his final appearance for the national team – and Nico Paz – the youngster who is widely tipped to inherit Messi's iconic number 10 jersey.

"It was a source of great pride for me to wear this jersey," Messi told fans in an address after the final whistle. "I can only express my gratitude... not coming back anymore will be deeply painful."
"Gracias, Leo!" read an intricate drone show in the sky above the stadium at full-time, which concluded with the drones forming a profile of Messi's face.

blocks.caption: Messi (left) also set up a goal for Nicolas Otamendi (19), who was also making his final appearance for ArgentinaImage: Matias Baglietto/REUTERS

blocks.text: Messi: 'Proud to be Argentinian'
Widely considered the best player of all time, Messi announced his retirement from international football on August 31 – barely a month after Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in the World Cup final.
"It was a decision which hurts and still hurts but I know it's the right time," he wrote in a statement composed just two days after the defeat in East Rutherford, USA.
"I swear that I have always given everything and that I have always fought for this shirt to make you happy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football," he said.
"Thank you, God for making me Argentinian."
Messi: following in the footsteps of Maradona

Argentina may have lost the 2026 World Cup final, but Messi's crowning moment came four years earlier when he led his nation to glory in Qatar, beating France on penalties after a spectacular final had ended 3-3.

The triumph crowned an international career which hadn't always been easy as Messi, so prolific in club football for Barcelona, struggled to live up to expectations in his home country, where fans worshipped him as the successor to the great Diego Maradona.

He announced his international retirement once before in 2016 after losing three consecutive finals with Argentina – the 2014 World Cup final vs. Germany in Brazil and the 2015 and 2016 Copa America finals, both to Chile.
But he reversed his decision and led his country to the Copa America title in 2021, ending Argentina's 28-year wait for a trophy, before finally winning the World Cup in 2022.
Messi may have retired from international football, but he still has a contract with his current club, Major League Soccer (MLS) side Inter Miami, until 2028.

articles.title: Unemployment eases to 5.3% in August 2026 as agriculture adds jobs
articles.summary: Manufacturing continues to weaken as employment in the sector further fell to 3.16 million in August from 3.43 million in July

blocks.text: UPLAND. Farmers harvest potatoes at a farm in Atok, Benguet, on March 31, 2026.
Manufacturing continues to weaken as employment in the sector further fell to 3.16 million in August from 3.43 million in July

items: The unemployment rate in the Philippines decreased to 5.3% in August 2026.
Employment gains were primarily seen in agriculture and forestry, while manufacturing continued to decline.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines’ unemployment rate eased to 5.3% in August 2026 as more Filipinos found work, particularly in the agriculture sector.
Around 2.77 million Filipinos were unemployed in August, down from 3.14 million in July, according to preliminary data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA).

The unemployment rate likewise fell from 6% in July, when it hit its highest level in more than four years. However, the August figure is worse than the 3.9% unemployment rate recorded in the same month of 2025.
National Statistician Dennis Mapa said the improvement from July was partly because fewer new entrants joined the labor force after the surge of fresh graduates looking for jobs the previous month.

Around 897,000 Filipinos joined the labor force for the first time in August, down from 1.5 million in July. Of these new entrants, around 470,000 were employed while 427,000 were unemployed, according to Mapa.

Agriculture and forestry accounted for the biggest month-on-month increase in employment, adding around 847,000 workers. Construction added another 390,000 jobs, while wholesale and retail trade gained 227,000.
Mapa said much of the agriculture increase came from rice and sugarcane production.

Manufacturing, however, continued to weaken. Employment in the sector fell to 3.16 million in August from 3.43 million in July and 3.46 million in June. Mapa said the electronics industry was among those affected, citing challenges in the global market, although seasonality may also be a factor.

blocks.caption: [READOUT] Where businesses can plug into the Luzon Corridor

blocks.text: Underemployment also improved month-on-month, falling to 11.9% in August from 12.9% in July. This meant around 5.9 million employed Filipinos still wanted additional working hours or another job. The rate, however, was higher than the 10.7% recorded in August 2025.

Bad weather also affected the quality of work during the month. Average hours worked fell to 39.2 hours a week from 40.6 hours in July, with millions of workers reporting bad weather as a reason for working fewer hours.
Mapa said shorter working hours could also translate to lower incomes for some workers, particularly the self-employed and those paid according to the amount of time they work.
The PSA expects employment to pick up toward the end of the year as businesses hire more seasonal workers ahead of the Christmas period. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Friends of Nolan Wells sue NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation
articles.summary:
Owens sued over September Instagram post that suggested trio tampered with evidence in death of Mississippi teen

Three friends of

blocks.text: Three friends of Nolan Wells, a Mississippi teen who died after a July boating trip, have sued NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation.

On 26 September, Owens shared an Instagram video that suggested Wells’s friends Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour had deleted evidence from Wells’s phone after his death, which the three men denied in their lawsuit.
“Arrest them immediately!! Like yesterday,” Owens captioned the post.

In a Monday complaint filed in a Mississippi district court, the fathers of the three young men, who are also named in the complaint as plaintiffs because they are deemed minors under state law, accuse Owens of harming their reputation and endangering their physical safety with the post.

“Due to the conduct of Owens and many other less-famous individuals, these completely innocent young men have been subjected to thousands of death threats, face-to-face harassment, and daily fear and ridicule from complete strangers. They’ve even been refused service at public establishments. Their lives, and the lives of their family members, will never be the same,” the complaint alleges.
Owens could not be immediately reached for comment.
The friends’ counsel also indicated they intend to take legal action against other public figures who have been vocal about Wells’s death including Al Sharpton and The View’s Sunny Hostin.
On 4 July, Wells and his friends sailed for a Mississippi island. He was last seen that afternoon. Two days later, his body was found on the island.

The circumstances of his death have fueled public suspicion. Wells, who was African American, had been partying with a mostly white friend group – a detail that gained traction online as some referenced Mississippi’s past with racial violence.

In late September, a Mississippi grand jury declined to file criminal charges, finding Wells’s death to appear “consistent with drowning”. Jackson county district attorney Angel Myers McIlrath has said Wells’s death was not racially motivated.

Wells’s parents and civil rights lawyer Ben Crump continue to call for further investigations, citing the state’s autopsy report, which said Wells’s airways and stomach were empty. His family has said the lack of water found undermines the drowning determination.

“I cannot take that ruling, and I cannot move on with my life,” Christine Wonsley, Wells’s mother, reportedly said, referring to the grand jury’s findings at a Monday press conference. “We have been left with more questions and heartbreak than any answers.”

articles.title: Agnés Callamard returns to Manila for Rappler’s Social Good Summit
articles.summary: The prominent French human rights expert, who former president Rodrigo Duterte once threatened to slap, is coming back to the Philippines for the first time since the lifting of a Duterte-era travel…

blocks.text: The prominent French human rights expert, who former president Rodrigo Duterte once threatened to slap, is coming back to the Philippines for the first time since the lifting of a Duterte-era travel ban

items: Agnés Callamard, previously banned from the Philippines by former president Duterte, returns to address the impact of unregulated artificial intelligence on human rights at Rappler's Social Good Summit 2026.
Callamard, now secretary general of Amnesty International, emphasizes the urgent need for humanity to regulate AI development to protect human values and freedoms.
The summit, taking place on November 21, will feature various speakers discussing the threats posed by AI, alongside Callamard's insights from her extensive human rights work.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Agnés Callamard, barred from setting foot in the Philippines by former president Rodrigo Duterte in 2018, returns to the Philippines for the first time to address an urgent global issue: how can we protect human rights and democracies from the threats posed by unregulated artificial intelligence (AI)?

Callamard, in her capacity as United Nations special rapporteur for extrajudicial killings during the Duterte presidency, had been outspoken about the conduct of his drug war, angering Duterte enough to ban her from the country.
In September this year, the Bureau of Immigration lifted the ban, paving the way for Callamard to return to the Philippines to speak at Rappler’s Social Good Summit 2026 happening on November 21.

Callamard, now secretary general of international human rights watchdog organization Amnesty International, will speak about the impact of artificial intelligence on human rights and basic freedoms at the summit.

Entitled, “WE THE HUMANS: Reclaim Our Future,” this year’s summit focuses on what humanity can still do to protect human values, human creativity, and human communities from the threats posed by unregulated and abused AI systems.

In recent months, rogue AI agents and words of warning coming even from the leaders of major AI companies and tech tycoons, point to an urgent need for humanity to come together to rein in AI development and protect human communities.

Without the proper guard rails, AI models pose an existential threat to humanity, supercharging wars and disinformation, compounding isolation, undermining critical thinking and learning abilities, and more.

The Social Good Summit is Rappler’s biggest annual fundraising event, with proceeds going to its investigative journalism and AI literacy initiatives. The summit will happen on November 21 at Shangri-La The Fort, Manila. Other speakers include AI Singapore’s Leslie Teo (also a member of the UN scientific panel on AI), historian Yuval Noah Harari (virtual), Rappler CEO and 2021 Nobel laureate Maria Ressa, and more. (READ: Learn, connect, be human: Social Good Summit unveils AI masterclasses)

Callamard is uniquely placed to speak about the global outlook of human rights, in the face of rapid AI development. She has led human rights investigations in over 30 countries, including the investigations into the murder of Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi. She has studied and written about women’s rights, freedom of expression, refugee movements, arbitrary killings, and more.

At Columbia University, she was director of the Global Freedom of Expression Project. She also served as executive director of the Freedom of Expression organization ARTICLE 19 and HAP International (the Humanitarian Accountability Partnership).

As secretary general of Amnesty International, she serves as its principal spokesperson. Amnesty International, one of the world’s largest non-governmental human rights organizations, has around 10 million supporters and offices in over 70 countries.

While she was UN rapporteur for extrajudicial killings, then-president Rodrigo Duterte threatened to slap her for “insulting” him with her words about his controversial anti-illegal drugs campaign. The Philippines’ own Commission on Human Rights said the president’s expletives and threats had a chilling effect on human rights defenders.

Today, Duterte is detained by the International Criminal Court in the Hague, Netherlands to stand trial for alleged crimes against humanity. His full-blown trial is set to begin on November 30. His anti-illegal drugs campaign resulted in at least 6,200 deaths in police operations alone by May 2022. Human rights organizations estimate that the number of fatalities could be as high as 30,000 to include those killed vigilante-style. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Trump says call scheduled with Putin to discuss possible plague death in Russia
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible case of plague at a Siberian research institute.

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump, left, and Russian President Vladimir Putin are seen in Alaska in August 2025. (Jae C. Hong/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible case of plague at a Siberian research institute.
WHO says Siberia case presents a 'very low' risk outside Russia

Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said he would be talking with Putin about the case "very soon." Health authorities are investigating after the death of an employee at an anti-plague institute, which authorities attributed to pneumonia with an unknown cause.

Asked what the U.S. intelligence community was saying about the case, Trump said the U.S. is in "very deep discussions" on the topic. "We'll be able to report about it, probably tomorrow," Trump said.

The World Health Organization on Tuesday said the case presents a "very low" risk outside Russia. The United Nations agency said it was in contact with Russian authorities following reports of the death last week of a woman who worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East.
On Monday, Trump said the U.S. would be willing to help Russia with the situation.
What we know about the suspected plague death in Russia

The call also comes as the Trump administration faces an Oct. 18 deadline to decide which Russian entities, if any, it will sanction under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which Trump signed into law on Sept. 18.
Ukraine has given the administration and Congress a wish list of Russian companies, vessels and individuals it would like to see hit with U.S. sanctions under that law.

articles.title: ‘Not exactly his favorite senator’: Susan Collins distances herself from Trump in Maine debate
articles.summary:
Republican challenged by Democrat Troy Jackson in critical Senate race says she opposes Iran war and Canada tariffs

Susan Collins, the Republican senator for Maine, pointedly distanced…

blocks.text: Susan Collins, the Republican senator for Maine, pointedly distanced herself from Donald Trump in a televised debate with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson on Tuesday, as she sought to present an image of independence in a state that has voted against Trump three times.

Proclaiming herself as not the US president’s “favorite senator”, Collins made the highly unusual boast for a Republican that she had voted with Joe Biden, a Democrat, more than 90% of the time when he was president. She also emphasized her differences with her fellow Republicans, saying she voted against her own party more than any other senator.

Collins’ defensiveness came amid a determined onslaught from Jackson, 58, a veteran former state legislator who was getting his first chance to present himself to a broad audience since replacing Graham Platner as the Democratic candidate in a contest that could be vital to the party’s hopes of winning the Senate.

Platner, a former harbor master, was forced to withdraw from the race in July after facing sexual assault allegations, which he denied, leaving Democrats racing against the clock to replace a candidate who had built up momentum campaigning on a populist progressive platform.

Jackson painted Collins as a Trump loyalist, saying she voted with the president 96% of the time. He also doggedly focused on her 2018 vote for the conservative supreme court justice Brett Kavanaugh, tying it to the court’s subsequent overturning of Roe v Wade, which had for half a century guaranteed the national right to abortion.

“Tonight is about who you stand with when it matters,” Jackson said in a pithy opening statement. “Eight years ago today, Maine women went to DC and begged Senator Collins not to confirm Brett Kavanaugh, but she did it anyways.
“He helped overturn Roe v Wade, and today she says she has no regrets. Would you trust her to pick the next supreme court justice?”

Collins, 73, who has been a senator since 1996, has frequently presented herself as a moderate who stands against more radical trends in her own party. The posture is in line with Maine’s profile as a more Democratic-leaning state, which Trump has not won in any of his three presidential campaigns and which has voted for Democrat presidential candidates in every election since 1992.

Nevertheless, Collins went to unusual lengths to differentiate herself from Trump on a range of issues, including the war with Iran, which she said she voted to end nine times, calling it “not well thought out”.
Collins reacted with something close to alarm when the moderator, Gregg Lagerquist, said Trump had suggested that the president might pay a campaign visit to Maine.

“I don’t think that President Trump is going to come to Maine,” she said. “He’s talking about going to a lot of different states. I’ve heard nothing from his office, and I’m not exactly his favorite senator.”
Collins stressed her differences with the president on specific issues pertinent to the Maine economy, including rural healthcare and tariffs against Canada, with which the state shares a border.
“I have been the most outspoken opponent of the tariffs on Canada,” she said. “Canada is not China. It’s our neighbor and our friends.”
Polls show the two candidates running neck and neck.

Leandro Leviste via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — A Makati Regional Trial Court (RTC) has issued a warrant of arrest against Rep. Leandro Leviste (Batangas 1st District) over alleged violations of the Public Service Act.
According to a copy of the warrant of arrest sent to reporters by the National Bureau of Investigation, the Makati RTC Branch 235 issued the warrant on October 5.

“You are hereby commanded to arrest LEANDRO ANTONIO L. LEVISTE, who is/are said to be found in/at N/A, PARAISO, CALATAGAN, BATANGAS, CALABARZON or elsewhere, and who has/have been charged before me with the offense of PUBLIC SERVICE ACT SECTION 25 OF COMMONWEALTH ACT NO. 146, AS AMENDED BY RA NO. 11659) and bring him/her/them forthwith before me to be dealt with according to law,” a portion of the warrant of arrest read.
The Makati court has set Leviste’s bail at P72,000.

This is part of the graft and plunder case being investigated by the Office of the Ombudsman against Leviste and his mother, Sen. Loren Legarda, over alleged irregularities involving solar energy projects and service contracts linked to Leviste’s companies.
Both Legarda and Leviste are said to be in France. According to lawyer Tony La Viña, Legarda’s spokesperson, she is on medical leave due to a lung illness.
La Viña also said that Legarda is undergoing treatment in France and that Leviste has been taking care of her.
This is a developing story.

articles.title: David Ellison denies he has ‘politicized’ Skydance despite close Trump links
articles.summary: Ellison admits ‘good relationship’ with administration in remarks to reporters about newly merged media company David Ellison, the chief executive of the newly formed media conglomerate Skydance,…

blocks.text: David Ellison, the chief executive of the newly formed media conglomerate Skydance, denied that he has “politicized” the company despite the close connection he has forged with Donald Trump’s White House over the 20 months of his administration.

“We have a good relationship with this administration,” Ellison acknowledged to reporters at a Tuesday press briefing focused on the now-consummated merger of Paramount Skydance and CNN parent company Warner Bros Discovery.

“I also had a really good relationship with President Biden. I have a good relationship with [Republican South Carolina senator] Tim Scott, and I have a good relationship with Governor Gavin Newsom. I think it is important to talk to everybody on both sides of the aisle … When you’re operating within a business-friendly administration, you should always have those relationships.”
“We want to speak to everybody,” Ellison added. “We do not want to politicize the company.”

Asked about his conversations with Trump about CNN, Ellison did not directly discuss his communications with the president, the network’s most prominent critic. But he said he wanted to clarify that “we have not talked to any political leader of any party about news, other than to say that we want to be in the truth business and we want to be in the trust business. And we believe in complete editorial independence.”

Amid concerns about whether Ellison might move CNN in a more rightward editorial direction, he said that both the cable news network and CBS News would be “completely editorially independent”, echoing a message he delivered earlier in the day during a town hall meeting with company employees.

Ellison also gave an endorsement to the two leaders he has tapped to continue running the two news networks networks he now controls, CNN chief executive Mark Thompson and CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss.
On Monday, Thompson told staffers in a memo that he would remain at the merged company, while Skydance also confirmed that Weiss would remain in her role.
“We’re thrilled, obviously, with Mark,” Ellison said. “We’re thrilled with Bari.”

Asked about a potential merging of CBS News and CNN and any cuts – or “synergies” – that might stem from that, Ellison said he and his leadership team would spend the next several months “basically getting under the hood on all of that”. Most of the $6bn in expected savings from the merger would not come from job losses, he said.
Ellison was not asked about Weiss’s performance as the editorial leader of CBS News. When asked specifically about Weiss’s performance by a Guardian reporter in June, Ellison ignored the question.

articles.title: Palace rejects VP Sara's claim that Marcos admin was behind cash delivery claims
articles.summary: “Wala nang masisira kay VP Sara; nasa katawan na niya ‘yan."

blocks.text: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and Vice President Sara Duterte on January 25, 2024.
STAR / KJ Rosales

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang dismissed Vice President Sara Duterte’s claims that the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was behind the multi-million-peso cash delivery allegations against her to undermine her reputation.
“Wala nang masisira kay VP Sara; nasa katawan na niya ‘yan,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in an interview on Tuesday, October 6, when asked to react to Duterte’s allegations.
(There’s nothing left to tarnish about Vice President Sara; it’s already on her.)

Earlier Tuesday, Duterte accused the Marcos administration and its communications officials of orchestrating efforts to damage her reputation and redirecting the president’s corruption issues toward her.
This came after dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. claimed that more than P2 billion in cash was delivered to her upon the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
Duterte denied the allegations anew and reiterated that she did not personally know Gracioso.
Pointing fingers
Castro said the vice president is just pointing fingers at others because she can no longer present valid evidence to debunk the allegations.
“Siguro ‘yun talaga ‘yung mangyayari kapag ka wala nang mahanap na pang-defense, magtuturo ka na lang ng iba. Wala pang naibibigay na ebidensiya na wala silang natanggap,” Castro said.
(Perhaps that’s what happens when you can’t find anything to defend yourself, you’ll point to others. No evidence has been presented to prove that they received nothing.)

The Palace spokesperson also answered Duterte’s claims that Gracioso’s statements are intended to support the alleged unexplained wealth allegations against her in the ongoing impeachment trial, saying that the vice president has failed to properly deny the allegations against her.
“So ang pangulo, lagi niyang itinuturo. Hindi kayang ibenta ng pangulo ang bansa sa dayuhan. Isa itong karumal-dumal na gawain, so ‘wag natin itong tularan,” Castro said.
(She’s always pointing to the president. The president cannot sell the country to foreigners. It’s a heinous act, so let’s not follow this.)

articles.title: Chinese state firms remitted P319 million to Sara Duterte-linked company — Hontiveros
articles.summary: The Anti-Money Laundering Council had previously flagged these transactions as covered and suspicious transaction reports due to a lack of legitimate underlying transactions.

blocks.text: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte gestures as she leaves the Hall of Justice in Quezon City, Metro Manila on Sept. 11, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — Chinese state-owned enterprises with direct ties to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and Beijing’s foreign influence apparatus have remitted millions of pesos to Cale88 Foods Corp., a company linked to Vice President Sara Duterte.
During the impeachment trial on October 6, Sen. Risa Hontiveros revealed that her office’s research uncovered deep geopolitical links behind the P319 million that entered Calle88 from China.
The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) had previously flagged these transactions as covered and suspicious transaction reports due to a lack of legitimate underlying transactions.
According to Hontiveros, one of the entities that sent money to Calle88 is China National Township Enterprises.

“Base po sa research ng opisina ko, dating directly under the Ministry of Agriculture sa China at naging isang large state-owned agricultural enterprise under the supervision of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council,” Hontiveros said.

(Based on my office’s research, it was previously directly under the Ministry of Agriculture in China and became a large state-owned agricultural enterprise under the supervision of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council.)
She added that the public profiles of China National Township Enterprises openly mention being "committed to serving the implementation of the country's Belt and Road Initiative and foreign policy.”

Another enterprise is Beijing Jianweifang Food Co., owned by the Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group, which acts as its Series A investor and has maintained a strategic cooperation agreement with the Beijing firm since 2019.
She said that the Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group is "not an ordinary company" but a Chinese state-owned enterprise that actively advances the interests of the CCP.

“It's a Chinese state-owned enterprise. It advances the interests of the Chinese Communist Party. Sa mismong corporate governance structure ng Xinjiang Fruit may institutional Chinese Communist Party organization na naka-embed,” Hontiveros said.

(It is a Chinese state-owned enterprise. It advances the interests of the Chinese Communist Party. Embedded within the very corporate governance structure of Xinjiang Fruit is an institutional Chinese Communist Party organization.)

When asked by Hontiveros whether the AMLC is actively investigating these Chinese companies and their geopolitical linkages, AMLC Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura said that he was unable to answer.
“The only documents related to what we were subpoenaed po 'yung pong mga na-submit po namin na…Summary report po, financial investigation report, financial investigation report,” Buenaventura said.
(The only documents related to what we were subpoenaed for are the ones we submitted, which are the summary report and the financial investigation reports.)
In a statement on October 5, the Chinese Embassy denied that Beijing had ties to a "Philippine political faction."
Calle88 was listed among the business interests connected with Sara Duterte in her 2022–2025 Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.
However, records from the Securities and Exchange Commission show that Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio, was an incorporator, director and shareholder of Calle88 from 2021 to 2024.
His ownership reportedly reached 47.5% in 2024, but his name no longer appeared as a shareholder in 2025.

articles.title: Christa Pike awake after failed Tennessee execution: lawyers
articles.summary: A death row inmate who survived a botched execution last week is conscious and talking in hospital, according to her lawyers, who want to commute her death sentence to life imprisonment without…

image.caption: Christa Pike was transported from prison to hospital after last week's botched executionImage: George Walker IV/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: A prisoner who survived an attempt to carry out the death penalty in Tennessee, the United States, last week is conscious and speaking as she continues to receive treatment in hospital.
"Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care," the inmate's attorneys said in a statement on Tuesday.
"Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed. Her recovery is medically unprecedented."

Pike, who was sentenced to death for the beating, stabbing and murder of a classmate in 1995, survived two doses of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital – which her lawyers said left her arms burned and blistered.
Christa Pike not 'free of further serious risk'
"She's still in the ICU," said Dr. Joel Zivot, a professor of anesthesiology and surgery in Atlanta in neighboring Georgia, who consulted as an expert for Pike's legal team.

"She has recovered to a certain degree that she's able to be off a ventilator and able to speak, but in no way would I announce her free of further serious risk. There's still a lot of bad things that can happen here, even when everyone is doing their job well."
Tuesday's updates were the first indication that Pike's condition has improved since the failed execution attempt at a Nashville prison last Wednesday.

Her attorneys thanked first responders and medical staff who they said have "treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her" – as they prepare to go to court on Wednesday seeking to learn more about what went wrong with the lethal injection.

blocks.caption: Christa Pike was sentenced to death on March 30, 1996 for her role as a teenager in the torture-murder of her 19-year-old schoolmateImage: WBIR-TV/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Pike's attorneys seeking to commute sentence
The lawyers are seeking a court order requiring the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve evidence, including drug lot numbers, records and other information from the attempted execution.
Ultimately, they are looking to have Pike's sentence commuted to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
While Dr. Zivot said Pike's current state "bodes well for a good recovery," her attorneys warned that her prognosis is still "unclear" and said she faces "a long recovery."
"Christa is a survivor and will take recovery one day at a time," they said.

According to the Death Penalty Information Center, which publishes data and analysis on capital punishment in the United States, Pike is the first prisoner ever to survive "after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs."

The aviation agency says the incident occurred around 10:30 a.m. local time as the Delta plane was taxiing for departure, and the Air Canada plane was being towed toward the gate.

The U.S. agency says the Delta plane's left wingtip clipped the Air Canada aircraft's horizontal stabilizer, a wing-likestructure at the tail of a plane.

articles.title: Plague epidemic risk in Russia low after death of lab technician, WHO says
articles.summary:
World Health Organization detects no sign of further outbreak since Darya Shipilova died last week

The World Health Organization has said the risk of an epidemic in Russia is low after the…

blocks.text: The World Health Organization has said the risk of an epidemic in Russia is low after the sudden death of a lab technician who worked at a plague research institute in Siberia.

Darya Shipilova, who was 28, died last week, two days after falling ill. Russian media reports suggested she may have become infected after an accident at her workplace, where dangerous pathogens are kept and studied.

Russian authorities have downplayed the incident and say Shipilova died of “pneumonia of an unknown aetiology”. Strict quarantine measures have been imposed at the research centre in the city of Irkutsk and in several neighbouring hospitals.

Christian Lindmeier, a WHO spokesperson, said on Tuesday that there was no sign of a wider outbreak. “All ‌of the patients’ contacts have reportedly been identified and are being monitored for ‌illness, and none to date have shown ​symptoms of illness,” he said.

Russian ⁠officials were still ​investigating whether viral pneumonic plague caused Shipilova’s death but the WHO had assessed the health risk as “moderate to low” for Irkutsk, “low” for the rest of Russia and “very low” for Europe, he said.
WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged Russia on Tuesday to be transparent about Shipilova’s death.

“Timely, complete and transparent information sharing under the International Health Regulations is essential to clarify conflicting reports and enable an accurate assessment of potential public health risks,” he wrote on X.

According to Russian media, 60 of Shipilova’s colleagues have been locked in the institute where she worked since Friday, sleeping on the floors and chairs while tests are carried out. Similar measures have been imposed in five hospitals, with relatives forbidden to see patients.

The Kremlin’s spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, urged people on Tuesday not to listen to rumours but to rely on statements from Russia’s health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor. It said the situation in Irkutsk was stable, with no new infectious disease cases reported among institute employees.

Washington has been watching developments closely. The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, called on Moscow on Tuesday to release more details about the case. “I think it’s incumbent upon ⁠Russia to obviously share more information with ​the world,” he said. “We’re watching it very closely, hour ‌by hour.”

The Wall Street Journal reported that the US state department had sent Russia a confidential diplomatic communication known as a demarche warning Moscow that failure to disclose details runs counter to its international health obligations.
Trump said on Tuesday that he was due to speak shortly with Russian president Vladimir Putin about the technician’s death.
